annotations.title: Generate a PIX copy-and-paste BRCode (EMVCo + CRC16)

description: Builds a static PIX copy-and-paste string following the Central Bank of Brazil EMVCo specification, with the CRC16-CCITT checksum already computed, from a PIX key plus receiver name and city. The returned brcode can be pasted into any Brazilian banking app or rendered as a QR code. Use it to charge for an order, issue a payment link, or settle an invoice in BRL. Do not use it to read an existing code (use br_decode_pix_brcode), and note that it builds the payload only: it does not register the charge with a bank, does not reserve an amount and cannot confirm that money arrived. Deterministic, read-only and fully offline, so the same arguments always return the same brcode and a retry neither duplicates a charge nor creates anything. Costs 0.01 USDC per call via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453) or a B2B X-API-Key; an unpaid call returns HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. Field limits mandated by the specification are enforced by truncation and accent stripping rather than by rejection, so always read back merchantName, merchantCity and txid to see what was actually encoded.

amount.description: Charge amount in BRL as a plain number, for example 149.9 for R$ 149,90. Omit it, or pass zero or a negative number, to issue an open-value code the payer fills in.

description.description: Optional free-text note shown to the payer. Accents are stripped and the value is truncated to 40 characters. Omitting it produces a shorter code.

key.description: The receiver's PIX key, used verbatim after trimming. Accepts any key type: CPF or CNPJ digits, an email address, a phone number in +55DDNNNNNNNNN form, or a random EVP UUID. The key is not verified against any bank, so a typo produces a syntactically valid code that will fail at payment time.

merchantCity.description: Receiver city. Accents are stripped and the value is truncated to the 15 characters the specification allows; an empty value becomes 'SAO PAULO'.

merchantName.description: Receiver name. Accents are stripped and the value is truncated to the 25 characters the specification allows; an empty value becomes 'RECEBEDOR'.

txid.description: Your transaction reference, echoed back by the bank in the settlement record and therefore the field to reconcile against. Whitespace is removed, accents are stripped and the value is truncated to 25 characters; defaults to '***'.

name: br_generate_pix_brcode

error.description: Stable machine-readable failure code, present only when the call itself was rejected. Common values: 'bad_request' (malformed JSON or no operation supplied), 'invalid_payment' / 'settlement_failed' (x402 verification or settlement refused, returned with HTTP 402), 'B2B_KEY_INVALID' and 'B2B_QUOTA_EXCEEDED' (B2B X-API-Key path), 'invalid_wafermap_signature' (marketplace HMAC path). A document that simply fails validation is NOT an error: the call returns success:true with valid:false inside the result block.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the failure, in Portuguese. Safe to log or surface to a human operator.

amountFormatted.description: The amount rendered in Brazilian format, for example 'R$ 149,90', or the literal 'Valor Aberto' when the code carries no fixed amount.

brcode.description: The complete copy-and-paste string, checksum included. Paste it into a banking app or encode it as a QR code.

crc16.description: The four hexadecimal CRC16-CCITT digits appended to the payload.

crcValid.description: Always true here, because the checksum was computed rather than read.

merchantCity.description: Receiver city as actually encoded, after accent stripping and truncation to 15 characters.

merchantName.description: Receiver name as actually encoded, after accent stripping and truncation to 25 characters.

txid.description: Transaction reference as actually encoded, after cleaning and truncation to 25 characters.

processingTimeMs.description: Edge processing time in milliseconds, excluding payment settlement. Mirrored in the X-Processing-Time-Ms response header.

success.description: true when the request was processed and paid for.

suggestedNextSteps.description: Chaining hints for autonomous agents: sibling paid APIs in the same suite that are commonly called right after this one. Purely advisory, never required.

endpoint.description: Absolute HTTPS endpoint of the suggested follow-up API.

priceUsdc.description: Price of the suggested follow-up call, in USDC.

tool.description: Tool name of the suggested follow-up API.

when.description: Condition under which the follow-up call is worth making.
